# Bleeding radiators

## Why I was doing it

First proper chilly week of Nov 2023. Back bedroom radiator hot at the bottom, stone cold across the top 15cm. Front room one gurgling like a drain. Classic air in the system. 9 radiators in the house, all steel panel ones except the old cast iron column one in the front room which weighs a ton.

## The routine

1. Heating ON for 20 minutes so everything's circulating, then heating OFF and wait till the pipes stop ticking (pumping while bleeding just pulls more air in)
2. Downstairs first, then up, furthest from the boiler first
3. Radiator key (the brass one on the hook in the meter cupboard, NOT the cheap one that rounds off the square) and a folded tea towel under the valve
4. Quarter turn, hiss, wait for a steady dribble of water, close
5. Back bedroom took ages, at least 40 seconds of hissing

## Pressure after

Boiler gauge was 1.5 bar before, 0.6 bar after bleeding all 9. That's why the boiler sulked. Topped back up to 1.2 bar with the filling loop under the boiler: both taps open slowly, watch the needle, close both. Ran the heating an hour, bled the back bedroom again (little bit more air), pressure settled at 1.1.

Main boiler stuff (service, settings, the EA fault) lives in [[Boiler service]].

## The weeping valve

April 2024 found the lockshield valve on the back bedroom rad weeping at the gland nut, slow drip onto a little dark ring on the carpet. That was where the pressure kept going. Nipped the gland nut up a quarter turn with a 19mm spanner, wrapped two turns of PTFE under it, fixed. Ollie had a look at the next service and was happy.

## Inhibitor

Since I'd been letting water out and putting fresh in, added Fernox F1 Protector, 500ml can, £14.50 from City Plumbing (Fishponds branch), injected through the towel rail bleed point with the Fernox injector. Should be good till the next drain down.

## Notes to self

- Bled again Oct 2024, only the back bedroom and the landing had any air. Pressure went 1.3 to 1.1
- TRV heads are Drayton TRV4, the back bedroom one sticks. Tap the pin with the handle of a screwdriver
- If the downstairs loo radiator ever needs to come off, see [[Painting the hallway]] for how I did the hallway one
